title: Humanoid robots boost DRAM demand; Samsung, SK hynix seize new growth
key_facts: Counterpoint Research projects DRAM demand from humanoid robots to rise more than 20-fold, from about 8,300 terabits this year to about 172,000 terabits in 2030.
Average DRAM per humanoid robot is expected to more than double, from 19 GB this year to 39 GB in 2030.
Battery-powered robots need low-power DRAM (LPDDR) and high-capacity NAND flash, so demand for those is also expected to rise.
Chosunbiz says this opens a new market for Samsung Electronics and SK hynix beyond the high-bandwidth memory (HBM) used in AI data centers.

Micron CEO Sanjay Mehrotra said at the company's earnings release on 30 Sep that Level 4 and higher self-driving vehicles typically carry over 200 GB of memory and several terabytes of storage, and predicted humanoid robots will need a similar level over the long term.
Counterpoint also expects more demand for compute chips such as Nvidia's GPUs as robot AI models advance.
quote_evidence: Demand for DRAM used in humanoid (human-shaped) robots is expected to grow more than 20-fold by 2030.
The average DRAM capacity per Humanoid Robot is expected to more than double, from 19 gigabytes (GB) this year to 39 GB in 2030.
For memory companies such as Samsung Electronics and SK hynix, this effectively opens a new market.
why_it_matters_hint: Humanoid robots could become a new customer group for memory makers beyond AI data centers, if robots are built in large numbers.
